Appearance:

Shri Arvind Kumar Dwivedi - Advocate for the petit  Shri Mohit Shivhare Ga appearing on behalf of Advo  1].
 Shri Sunil Singh Rawat, learned counsel for the re  ORDER
The applicant has filed this first bail application under Section 482 of BNSS/438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.

Applicant apprehends her arrest in connection with Crime no.240/2025 registered at Police Station Purani Chhawani, District Gwalior (M.P.) in relation to the offence punishable under Sections 420,
34 of IPC.
As per prosecution story, Neelam Rathore had executed an agreement in February 2022 with the applicant Chandni Sharma and her husband Akash Devolia to purchase a house owned by her for Rs 18 lakhs.

Akash Devolia had told her that there is a loan of Rs 14 lakhs on the said house of Shubh Finance Company, and after depositing the remaining amount out of Rs 14 lakhs with the finance company, he will register the said house in her name.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20617 2 MCRC-39948-2025

From time to time,
Akash and Chandni received an amount of Rs 10 lakhs from her.

The remaining amount of Rs 8 lakh was to be paid to the applicant at the time of registration which was to be got done within 11 months Smt Chandani Sharma D/O Shri Mahendra ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113862001/
1 from 13-04-2023 and in the said period, the applicant was required to pay whatever loan they have from Shubham Finance in addition to Rs 8 lakh.

sentences.text: On 14-02-2024, when the husband of complainant had gone out on work, the employees of Shubham Finance came to the house and told that there is a loan of Rs 14 lakh on the house which Akash has not deposited and took possession of the said house and got it vacated from the complainant.
On the basis of which, the above crime was registered.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that it is purely a civil dispute between the parties as no registered sale deed was got executed by the applicant and her husband though possession was given and also though it was admitted in the agreement that the house was mortgaged but the loan was not repaid to the Bank.
It is further submitted that there is no previous case between the applicant and the complainant.
It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of District Gwalior and there is no likelihood of her absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in investigation/trial and would not be a source of embarrassment and harassment in any manner to the complainant party side.
The applicant is ready to abide by all the terms and condition as imposed by this Court.
Under these grounds, learned counsel prayed for anticipatory bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20617 3 MCRC-39948-2025 Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application.
Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the above submissions and facts situation of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court intends to allow the application, therefore, it is hereby directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.
Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of Arresting Authority/Investigating Officer.
4. The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused;
5. The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial;
